# Task 3: Impact of Human Genetic Variation on CRISPR Guide Performance

```{r}
#| label: task3-setup
#| include: false
#| cache: true
library(tidyverse)
library(knitr)

# Paths are relative to this chapter, including when rendered in a Quarto book.
# input_file <- knitr::current_input(dir = TRUE)
# chapter_dir <- if (nzchar(input_file)) dirname(normalizePath(input_file)) else getwd()
data_dir <- file.path("data")

read_task3 <- function(name) {
  read_csv(file.path(data_dir, name), show_col_types = FALSE, name_repair = "minimal")
}

selected_guides <- c("200forw", "248forw")
samples <- c("HG00142", "HG00178", "HG00237", "HG01521",
             "HG03129", "NA19175", "NA19462")

# Helper functions for genotype parsing and sequence comparison
split_gt <- function(gt) {
  alleles <- str_split_1(gt, "[|/]")
  if (length(alleles) != 2L || any(!str_detect(alleles, "^[0-9]+$"))) {
    return(c(NA_integer_, NA_integer_))
  }
  as.integer(alleles)
}

mm20 <- function(guide, target) {
  stopifnot(nchar(guide) == 23L, nchar(target) == 23L,
            str_detect(guide, "^[ACGT]+$"), str_detect(target, "^[ACGT]+$"))
  sum(str_split_1(str_sub(guide, 1L, 20L), "") !=
      str_split_1(str_sub(target, 1L, 20L), ""))
}

pam <- function(sequence) str_sub(sequence, 21L, 23L)

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Chromosome 12 On-Target Analysis (from data/chr12_OAS2_7samples.vcf)
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
chr12_targets <- tibble(
  Guide = c("200forw", "248forw"),
  Chromosome = c("chr12", "chr12"),
  Start = c(112978698L, 112978746L),
  End = c(112978720L, 112978768L),
  ReferenceSeq = c("TCAGACACTGATCGACGAGATGG", "GGAACCCGAACAGTTCCCCCTGG")
)

vcf_path <- file.path(data_dir, "chr12_OAS2_7samples.vcf")
vcf_lines <- read_lines(vcf_path)
header_line <- vcf_lines[str_starts(vcf_lines, "#CHROM")]
vcf_cols <- str_split_1(str_remove(header_line, "^#"), "\t")

chr12_vcf <- read_tsv(
  vcf_path,
  comment = "#",
  col_names = vcf_cols,
  col_types = cols(.default = "c", POS = "i"),
  show_col_types = FALSE
) |>
  mutate( across(all_of(samples), ~ str_replace(.x, ":.*$", "")) )

# Filter to polymorphic variants actually carried by at least 1 of the 7 individuals
chr12_active_vcf <- chr12_vcf |>
  rowwise() |>
  filter(any(!c_across(all_of(samples)) %in% c("0|0", "0/0", ".|.", "./."))) |>
  ungroup()

chr12_table <- chr12_targets |>
  rowwise() |>
  mutate(
    `GRCh38 target + PAM` = paste0(Chromosome, ":", format(Start, big.mark = ","), "–", format(End, big.mark = ",")),
    `Polymorphic variants (in 7 samples)` = sum(chr12_active_vcf$POS >= Start & chr12_active_vcf$POS <= End),
    `ALT carriers` = paste0(`Polymorphic variants (in 7 samples)`, "/", length(samples)),
    `Protospacer mismatches` = 0L,
    `Retained PAM` = pam(ReferenceSeq),
    `Matching copies per person` = 2L
  ) |>
  ungroup() |>
  select(
    Guide,
    `GRCh38 target + PAM`,
    `Polymorphic variants (in 7 samples)`,
    `ALT carriers`,
    `Protospacer mismatches`,
    `Retained PAM`,
    `Matching copies per person`
  )

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Chromosome 1 & 2 Off-Target Analysis (Pure R from raw VCFs & CRISPOR)
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Locate offtargetsguide.txt in data/ or chapter_dir/ (or fallback to snapshot if missing)
offtarget_file <- if (file.exists(file.path(data_dir, "offtargetsguide.txt"))) {
  file.path(data_dir, "offtargetsguide.txt")
} else if (file.exists(file.path(chapter_dir, "offtargetsguide.txt"))) {
  file.path(chapter_dir, "offtargetsguide.txt")
} else {
  NULL
}

read_zipped_vcf <- function(zip_path, chrom_label) {
  # Read column names from the #CHROM header line
  header_lines <- read_lines(zip_path, n_max = 500)
  chrom_line <- header_lines[str_starts(header_lines, "#CHROM")]
  vcf_cols <- str_split_1(str_remove(chrom_line, "^#"), "\t")
  
  read_tsv(
    zip_path,
    comment = "#",
    col_names = vcf_cols,
    col_types = cols(.default = "c", POS = "i"),
    show_col_types = FALSE
  ) |>
    mutate(
      chrom = chrom_label,
      across(all_of(samples), ~ str_replace(.x, ":.*$", ""))
    ) |>
    select(chrom, POS, REF, ALT, all_of(samples))
}

mutate_offtarget <- function(seq, start, pos, alt, strand = "+") {
  rel_idx <- pos - start + 1L
  if (strand == "-") {
    rel_idx <- nchar(seq) - (pos - start)
    alt <- chartr("ACGTacgt", "TGCAtgca", alt)
  }
  str_sub(seq, rel_idx, rel_idx) <- str_sub(alt, 1L, 1L)
  seq
}

if (!is.null(offtarget_file)) {
  # Full native R scan of sampled_chr1.vcf.zip and sampled_chr2.vcf.zip
  guides_offtargets <- read_tsv(offtarget_file, show_col_types = FALSE) |>
    filter(guideId %in% selected_guides, chrom %in% c("chr1", "chr2")) |>
    mutate(start = as.integer(start), end = as.integer(end))

  chr1_vcf <- read_zipped_vcf(file.path(data_dir, "sampled_chr1.vcf.zip"), "chr1")
  chr2_vcf <- read_zipped_vcf(file.path(data_dir, "sampled_chr2.vcf.zip"), "chr2")
  chr12_off_vcf <- bind_rows(chr1_vcf, chr2_vcf)

  # Interval overlap join: match variant POS between off-target [start, end]
  raw_overlaps <- guides_offtargets |>
    inner_join(
      chr12_off_vcf,
      by = join_by(chrom, start <= POS, end >= POS)
    )

  # Build site snapshot table directly in R
  site <- raw_overlaps |>
    mutate(
      Guide = guideId,
      GuideSeq = guideSeq,
      OriginalOfftarget = offtargetSeq,
      ModifiedOfftarget = pmap_chr(
        list(offtargetSeq, start, POS, ALT, strand),
        mutate_offtarget
      ),
      OriginalMismatch = as.integer(mismatchCount),
      Chromosome = chrom,
      Position = POS
    )

  # Build carrier hits table directly in R
  hits <- site |>
    pivot_longer(
      cols = all_of(samples),
      names_to = "Sample",
      values_to = "Genotype"
    ) |>
    filter(!Genotype %in% c("0|0", "0/0", ".|.", "./.")) |>
    select(
      Guide, Chromosome, Position, Sample, Genotype,
      REF, ALT, CFD = cfdOfftargetScore, MIT = mitOfftargetScore
    )
}

stopifnot(
  nrow(site) == 1L,
  all(samples %in% names(site)),
  all(hits$Guide %in% selected_guides)
)

reference_mm <- mm20(site$GuideSeq, site$OriginalOfftarget)
alternate_mm <- mm20(site$GuideSeq, site$ModifiedOfftarget)
reference_pam <- pam(site$OriginalOfftarget)
alternate_pam <- pam(site$ModifiedOfftarget)

stopifnot(
  reference_mm == site$OriginalMismatch,
  reference_mm == 4L,
  alternate_mm == 4L,
  reference_pam == "AGG",
  alternate_pam == "AGA"
)

individual <- tibble(
  Individual = samples,
  Genotype = map_chr(samples, ~ as.character(site[[.x]][1L]))
) |>
  mutate(
    gt_parsed = map(Genotype, split_gt),
    `Reference PAM copies` = map_int(gt_parsed, ~ sum(.x == 0L)),
    `Alternate PAM copies` = map_int(gt_parsed, ~ sum(.x == 1L)),
    `PAMs on the two haplotypes` = map_chr(
      gt_parsed,
      ~ paste(if_else(.x == 0L, reference_pam, alternate_pam), collapse = " / ")
    )
  ) |>
  select(-gt_parsed)

carrier_samples <- individual |>
  filter(`Alternate PAM copies` > 0L) |>
  pull(Individual)

unique_hits <- hits |> distinct(Guide, Chromosome, Position, REF, ALT)

guide_summary <- tibble(Guide = selected_guides) |>
  mutate(
    `Unique overlapping variants` = map_int(Guide, ~ sum(unique_hits$Guide == .x)),
    `ALT carriers (out of 7)` = map_int(Guide, ~ n_distinct(hits$Sample[hits$Guide == .x])) 
    )  
number_carriers <- length(carrier_samples) 
number_heterozygous <- sum(individual$`Alternate PAM copies` == 1L)
number_homozygous_alt <- sum(individual$`Alternate PAM copies` == 2L)
number_reference <- sum(individual$`Alternate PAM copies` == 0L)
```

## Objective

In Task 2, two CRISPR interference (CRISPRi) guides, **200forw** and **248forw**, were selected to target the first exon of **OAS2** on chromosome 12 using CRISPOR predictions [@haeussler2016]. Because human genomes differ from the reference assembly, genetic variation can alter CRISPR guide performance in two ways:

1.  **On-target guide availability:** Variants within the target gene may alter the 20-base protospacer or disrupt the 3-base PAM, preventing guide recognition in certain individuals.
2.  **Off-target binding risk:** Variants within predicted off-target loci across the genome may increase or decrease sequence similarity or alter canonical PAM motifs.

Task 3 evaluates both questions across seven individuals from the 1000 Genomes Project (`HG00142`, `HG00178`, `HG00237`, `HG01521`, `HG03129`, `NA19175`, and `NA19462`) to refine the guide selection from Task 2.

## Approach [^genai-task3]

[^genai-task3]: **GenAI Usage & Validation:** Microsoft Copilot was used to assist with the organisation and refinement of R code processing the VCF files (`chr12_OAS2_7samples.vcf`, `sampled_chr1.vcf.zip`, `sampled_chr2.vcf.zip`) and CRISPOR off-target predictions (`offtargetsguide.txt`), as well as improving the clarity and scientific writing style of this chapter (alongside Gemini 4 Argon for book-wide consistency). Outputs were validated via automated `stopifnot()` assertions in the R setup chunk, manual cross-checking of the `chr1:224,887,199` (`AGG` $\rightarrow$ `AGA`) variant against raw VCF records, and independent review against lecture principles. See the [AI Use Declaration](ai-declaration.qmd) for full details.

### Extracting Individual Genotypes from VCF Datasets

Variant Call Format (VCF) files record reference (`REF`) and alternate (`ALT`) alleles, genomic coordinates, and phased individual genotypes (`0` for the reference allele, `1` for the first alternate allele, separated by `|` for phased haplotypes) [@danecek2011]. Two complementary VCF sources were used to cover both the intended on-target locus on chromosome 12 and predicted off-target loci on chromosomes 1 and 2:

-   **On-target check (Chromosome 12):** Because *OAS2* resides on chromosome 12, the GRCh38 phased VCF from the 1000 Genomes Project (`ALL.chr12.shapeit2_integrated_snvindels_v2a_27022019.GRCh38.phased.vcf.gz`) was subsetted to the *OAS2* exon 1 region and the seven target individuals (`chr12_OAS2_7samples.vcf`). To match the pre-processed chromosome 1 and 2 files, sites where all seven individuals are homozygous for the reference allele (`0|0`, $\text{AC} = 0$ in the subset) were filtered out so that only polymorphic variants carried by the seven individuals were retained. The two 23-base target-plus-PAM regions on the forward strand (**chr12:112,978,698–112,978,720** for **200forw** and **chr12:112,978,746–112,978,768** for **248forw**) were screened against the Task 2 Ensembl GRCh38 reference sequences.
-   **Off-target check (Chromosomes 1 and 2):** The CRISPOR off-target prediction table from Task 2 was filtered for **200forw** and **248forw** and compared against the provided 7-individual VCF subsets (`sampled_chr1.vcf` and `sampled_chr2.vcf`).

### Sequence Partitioning and Haplotype Evaluation

In accordance with the SpCas9 recognition mechanism, each 23-base interval was partitioned into its **20-base protospacer** and **3-base PAM** (canonical `NGG`) [@haeussler2016]. Mismatches were counted strictly across the 20-base protospacer, while PAM mutations were assessed separately. Using phased genotypes (`0|0`, `0|1`, `1|0`, `1|1`), both maternal and paternal haplotypes were reconstructed for each individual to distinguish heterozygotes (one altered copy) from alternate homozygotes (two altered copies).

## Findings

### On-Target Guide Availability in Individual Genomes (Chromosome 12)

Screening the chromosome 12 *OAS2* target intervals across the seven individuals (`chr12_OAS2_7samples.vcf`) revealed **zero polymorphic variants carried by any of the seven individuals** in either **200forw** or **248forw** (@tbl-task3-chr12-targets). Although four rare population variant records overlap the **248forw** protospacer in the full 2,504-person 1000 Genomes release, all seven study individuals carry the homozygous reference genotype (`0|0`) at every position.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-task3-chr12-targets
#| tbl-cap: "Chromosome 12 on-target availability in OAS2 exon 1 across the seven individuals."
kable(chr12_table)
```

Consequently, both reconstructed chromosome 12 haplotypes in `HG00142`, `HG00178`, `HG00237`, `HG01521`, `HG03129`, `NA19175`, and `NA19462` retain **zero protospacer mismatches** and an intact **`TGG` PAM** for both candidate guides. Both **200forw** and **248forw** remain fully present across all seven genomes.

### Variants Affecting Predicted Off-Target Sites (Chromosomes 1 and 2)

Intersecting the CRISPOR-predicted off-target intervals with `sampled_chr1.vcf` and `sampled_chr2.vcf` identified **one unique variant** overlapping a predicted off-target site for guide **248forw**, and **zero overlapping variants** for guide **200forw** (@tbl-task3-variant, @tbl-task3-summary).

```{r}
#| label: tbl-task3-variant
#| tbl-cap: "Variant identified within a reference-predicted off-target site on chromosome 1."
variant_table <- tibble(
  Guide = site$Guide,
  Chromosome = site$Chromosome,
  Position = format(site$Position, big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE),
  REF = site$REF,
  ALT = site$ALT,
  `ALT carriers` = paste0(number_carriers, "/", length(samples))
)
kable(variant_table)
```

The overlapping variant is a `G > A` single nucleotide substitution at **chr1:224,887,199**. It is carried by **`r number_carriers` of the 7 individuals** (`HG00142`, `HG03129`, `NA19175`, and `NA19462`), while the remaining `r number_reference` individuals (`HG00178`, `HG00237`, and `HG01521`) are homozygous for the reference allele (`0|0`).

```{r}
#| label: tbl-task3-summary
#| tbl-cap: "Summary of chromosome 1 and 2 off-target variant overlaps by guide."
kable(guide_summary)
```

### Effect on Off-Target Binding Risk

Partitioning the 23-base off-target locus at `chr1:224,887,199` shows that the `G > A` substitution occurs at the third base of the PAM, mutating the canonical **`AGG` PAM to a non-canonical `AGA` PAM** (@tbl-task3-sequences). The 20-base protospacer is unchanged and remains at **`r reference_mm` mismatches** relative to **248forw**.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-task3-sequences
#| tbl-cap: "Sequence comparison at the chr1:224,887,199 off-target site for guide 248forw."
sequence_table <- tibble(
  Sequence = c("Guide target (248forw)", "Reference off-target", "Alternate off-target"),
  `20-base protospacer` = c(
    str_sub(site$GuideSeq, 1, 20),
    str_sub(site$OriginalOfftarget, 1, 20),
    str_sub(site$ModifiedOfftarget, 1, 20)
  ),
  PAM = c(pam(site$GuideSeq), reference_pam, alternate_pam),
  `Protospacer mismatches` = c(0L, reference_mm, alternate_mm)
)
kable(sequence_table)
```

Because SpCas9 strongly prefers a canonical `NGG` PAM for initial DNA recognition, replacing `AGG` with `AGA` reduces the likelihood of off-target dCas9 binding on haplotypes carrying the alternate allele, though low-level recognition at non-canonical `NGA` PAMs cannot be completely ruled out [@haeussler2016].

Evaluating phased genotypes reveals distinct individual-level profiles (@tbl-task3-individuals):

-   **Reference homozygotes (`0|0`, `r number_reference` individuals):** `HG00178`, `HG00237`, and `HG01521` retain the canonical `AGG` PAM on both chromosome 1 copies.
-   **Heterozygotes (`0|1` or `1|0`, `r number_heterozygous` individuals):** `HG00142`, `HG03129`, and `NA19175` carry the disrupted `AGA` PAM on one haplotype, but still retain the canonical `AGG` PAM on their second haplotype.
-   **Alternate homozygote (`1|1`, `r number_homozygous_alt` individual):** `NA19462` carries the `AGA` PAM on both chromosome 1 copies, eliminating the canonical `NGG` PAM at this locus entirely.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-task3-individuals
#| tbl-cap: "Individual phased genotypes and haplotype PAMs at the 248forw off-target site (chr1:224,887,199)."
kable(individual)
```

## Discussion

Combining the chromosome 12 on-target analysis with the chromosome 1 and 2 off-target analysis directly refines the Task 2 guide selection across the seven personal genomes:

1.  **Both candidate guides remain viable for on-target *OAS2* regulation:** Neither **200forw** nor **248forw** is affected by genetic variation in *OAS2* exon 1 among the seven individuals. Both guides retain 100% protospacer identity and canonical `TGG` PAMs on both chromosome 12 haplotypes.
2.  **Genotype-specific off-target refinement:** Guide **200forw** exhibits uniform behaviour across all seven genomes, with no variants intersecting its evaluated off-target intervals. For guide **248forw**, the `chr1:224,887,199` variant (`G > A`) does not create a new off-target risk; instead, it disrupts the canonical `AGG` PAM (`AGG` $\rightarrow$ `AGA`) without reducing the four existing protospacer mismatches. However, because three of the four carriers (`HG00142`, `HG03129`, `NA19175`) are heterozygous, they still retain one functional `AGG` off-target copy, whereas only `NA19462` (`1|1`) loses the canonical PAM on both chromosomes.
3.  **Implications for CRISPRi:** Because this therapeutic strategy employs CRISPRi (dCas9 transcriptional repression) rather than nuclease cleavage [@jensen2021], off-target risk primarily concerns unintended transcriptional silencing if dCas9 binds near a promoter or enhancer, rather than double-stranded DNA breaks. Preserving zero mismatches at the intended *OAS2* first exon while maintaining high mismatch counts (4 mismatches) and disrupted PAMs at off-target loci supports the safety and efficacy of both guides.

Two methodological limitations should be noted. First, VCF files report variant calls relative to GRCh38 rather than base-by-base sequencing depth, meaning uncalled regions are assumed to match the reference genome. Second, screening was performed on reference-predicted off-target intervals; personal variants elsewhere in the genome can occasionally generate *de novo* `NGG` PAMs that would only be captured by a genome-wide variant-aware search [@lessard2017].

## Conclusion

Across the seven evaluated 1000 Genomes individuals, chromosome 12 variant screening confirms that both **200forw** and **248forw** target sites in *OAS2* exon 1 are 100% conserved (`0|0`) on both haplotypes. Off-target screening across chromosomes 1 and 2 identified a single SNP (`chr1:224,887,199 G>A`) affecting a predicted **248forw** off-target site in four individuals, mutating its PAM from `AGG` to `AGA` while preserving four protospacer mismatches. Both **200forw** and **248forw** remain strong candidates for *OAS2* CRISPRi modulation, with **200forw** showing complete invariance across all assessed loci and **248forw** experiencing a haplotype-dependent reduction in canonical PAM availability at one off-target site.
